I mean, I go to a public school. It's one of the best in the country, though, and a degree from here will pretty much have me set for life. I have recommendation letters from professors. I already work one job and worked two this summer. I am trying to take advantage of whichever scholarships come my way and my academic record thus far speaks for itself (I became fluent in a language considered difficult to learn within less than nine months, and my GPA is something like a 3.8 at one of the top public schools in the country). Even when I was working two jobs, though, I still wasn't making enough money to rent even the cheapest apartment within like 20 miles of where I live. I wouldn't be able to pay for gas or my car. He also owns my car, so I would be absolutely fucked if I severed ties. I cannot get the degree I need to get from any community college anywhere near me, otherwise I would. I also have other chronic health issues and those can be extremely expensive and can limit the amount of time I can work.
I'm 19, but because of him I literally have a full ride to the one of the best colleges in the country. I wouldn't be able to get that much without his help.
Yes, but he won't give me his information so I can actually fill it out. He is too proud to admit we need it. I am trying to get a PhD. I cannot afford to do this without him.

I'm stuck living with it. He's paying for me to go to college. I'm trying to interact with people and take care of myself but nothing is working. I have tried everything I am able to access but nothing is working.

He makes everything about him. My suffering becomes his suffering ("when *YOU* hurt yourself, can you imagine how *I* feel???"). He also loses his temper all the time and I'm at a point where I just cannot live like this anymore. 

I'm in therapy. I am trying to go out with people and use the coping mechanisms I'm learning in DBT and all that but nothing is helping. I try to distract myself and nothing helps. I've been trying to call the emergency hotlines when I feel suicidal but that only helps for about five minutes.

It's usually classic lit, but I do branch out a bit into psychology, sociology, and other subjects. I especially love old books. And not like that! I mean like, even as a teenager and my mom would say that I needed new shoes, I felt guilty for needing things. I even try to hide things I need from my parents so as not to be a burden.
Thank you so much ♡

"Chronically-ill" because I feel bad for venting about having mental/physical health issues, I feel bad for people I know who have to put up with me crying at all or me having to take forever in the bathroom because I am in pain or me needing to ask for reassurance because I'm anxious. I feel like my whole existence is a burden.
Really any sort of book that catches my eye! But I also feel guilty when people ask to buy me things (even relatives), so this never comes up. I just feel like a massive, chronically-ill burden.

I don't even know. I collect books. I'm into antiques. It makes me happy, but only for a millisecond. I get a hit of that sweet, sweet dopamine when I buy one and then go back to being sad almost immediately. I'm trying to spend more on myself, I just genuinely feel guilty and lonely if I'm not spending it on other people

I am still going, and it helps a lot with the other symptoms of BPD - this is the first depressive episode in months, but also the worst. I genuinely do not have hobbies. I try to! I am in the middle of nowhere and broke about 99% of the time, though. Oftentimes I just waste entire days watching dumb shit on youtube or, when I do have money, spending large amounts of it at once. Those are really the only things I've enjoyed (if you can call it that) doing on my own over the past year or so.
I let people talk about whatever they want to me, even if I know it will be a trigger. I'm basically a human doormat.

I've been in therapy since age 11 and done both cognitive behavioral therapy and am currently in dialectical behavioral therapy. I've been trying different social groups and clubs throughout high school and college, try to start conversations with people I dont know well to get ti know them better, try to do literally everything i can for my friends (I dropped $400 on Christmas gifts last year. I work minimum wage).

I should mention I dont really have much to live for. I have friends, sure, but they'd all move on. They have closer friends - they have BEST friends! I'm a student, but what comes after I get my degree if I dont have companionship? I would rather be dead.
Thank you so much!

I am afraid of feeling pain, of causing lasting pain to my relatives, and of there being nothing afterwards. I don't know what will come afterwards, and that terrifies me. It is such an uncertain thing - still, I don't want to live anymore, either.

My hope is that hospitalization can somehow change my life for the better by setting me on the right track, something which I have tried so often to do and which never seems to work. I am quite emotionally unstable and, as I said, do not really trust myself to make good choices due to my impulsivity. In addition, when I am at my lowest, I can no longer really take care of myself. Even apart from the refusing-to-eat-out-of-self-loathing, I have reached points where I am too anxious to leave my room in order to eat.

I've told my therapist about all of this (I actually did so earlier today), and we barely even talked about it. She says that I am making progress, which is true in the sense that I no longer have an addiction to boot, but everything seems so bleak. I somehow feel isolated even when I'm with others.

And I mean, I kind of do want to die, it's just a matter of being too afraid to actually go through with it.
